paragraphs: Four travellers once reached a tall wall standing across their path.

The first one struggled his way to the top and dropped over the other side without a single glance back. The second scrambled up, peered over, gave a cry of joy and vanished too. The third climbed up, saw where his friends had gone, burst out laughing with happiness and jumped after them.
The fourth also reached the top. But instead of leaping, he turned around and came back down, so that he could tell the others what had become of his companions.

Swamiji explained the picture. The wall is Maya, the veil that hides the deeper reality from us. The great souls who have crossed it seldom return, and their joyful laughter, echoing back over the wall, is our proof that something wonderful lies beyond. And a rare few, like the fourth traveller, come back on purpose to show the rest of us the way.
learn: When you have found something good, whether a skill, a truth or a way out of a hard place, you have a choice: keep going alone or turn back and help others climb. The people we remember most are usually the ones who came back.
